Wayback if you aren't familiar with it (I know I'm not) is a fuse filesystem that you point to a base file system. It then functions the same as the original except that it provides all versions of your files.

I like that it doesn't require you to make a partition and transfer data to it like zfs or btrfs would to get their features (not that they solve this problem). I still am willing to try less lightweight solutions but from my survey of the topic it seems that everything is dated / defunct projects.

At the high level what I to do is build is a detached system that can be rsynced to, mirror everything on a system in home var etc, and then store it versioned. It seems like because that would have a lot of value either it does exist but I live under a rock or everyone who has tried so far has failed.
Wayback hasn't been worked on since 2013. Any realistic automatic versioning systems out there?

I used Syncthing for a while to accomplish the sync'ing aspect of what you're talking about, and while I haven't set it back up since a major systems wipe some time ago, and then never in this capacity, I did find documentation that suggests it may support the versioning component you seek.

I use rdiff-backup to handle my versioned backups. rsnapshot is a bit faster and simpler for looking through old increments. I'm not sure if either of these are better than what you've already looked at though. I like them, but they don't work automatically like a versioned filesystem.
